A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoArena and retain matching central experiments and case studies. All pages, including appendices, support comparison despite substantial retitling, rewriting, and reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original model rankings, pairwise voting results, expert agreement, style analysis, model–human alignment, and dataset composition statistics.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds prompt-classification outcomes in Appendix A.1 and style-adjusted model rankings in Appendix A.7.

M1.justification: v4 Section 4.1 and Figure 2 introduce an LLM-based prompt-relevance gate before model battles, whereas v3 describes manual relevance filtering. Pairwise voting and Bradley–Terry ranking remain unchanged. Appendix A.1 presents filtering as a feasibility study, leaving actual deployment unclear.

E1.justification: v4 adds binary classification of geolocation versus general-purpose prompts, using GeoArena and Chatbot Arena prompts in Appendix A.1. The original image coverage and case studies are retained; removing the GeoArena-1K name does not establish removal of its underlying data.

E2.justification: The new filtering study evaluates Gemini 2.0 flash, GPT 3.5 turbo, and GPT 4.1 mini. The original 17-model leaderboard and two-model alignment comparison retain their participants. GeoChain's addition to Table 1 is contextual comparison, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a 200-prompt classification protocol: 100 GeoArena positives and 100 Chatbot Arena negatives, assessed by accuracy. v4 also reports automated plus manual input filtering, replacing v3's manual-only description. The retained expert/alignment sample sizes and unchanged appendix alignment prompt do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v4 adds a complete style-adjusted leaderboard that exposes substantial sensitivity of model ordering to stylistic confounds, extending v3's coefficient-only reporting from its existing style regression. It also adds automatic-filter feasibility testing. Existing expert reliability analyses and difficult/additional cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same primary leaderboard confidence intervals using 100 bootstrap rounds and 95% coverage. No new seed information, repeated-run counts, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced; the added adjusted leaderboard reports point estimates.

E6.justification: v4 Table 6 adds substantially reordered style-adjusted results, including Gemma 3 12B at 932.11 and ninth place, versus fourth in the retained unadjusted ranking. Appendix A.1 reports 100% classification accuracy for all three filters. Original leaderboard values, agreement scores, style coefficients, and dataset proportions remain unchanged; adjusted scores are not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: New Section 3 defines image, prompt, response, and human-expectation spaces and an expected reasoning-alignment functional in Equation 1. The Elo and Bradley–Terry mathematics remains equivalent despite notation changes and consolidation. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v3 centers an open worldwide-image-geolocalization platform addressing leakage and GPS-related privacy. v4 centers a formal framework for open-world geographic reasoning, emphasizing reasoning alignment and ambiguous or unavailable ground truth. The explicit dataset-release contribution is replaced by a general platform-release contribution.

C2.justification: v4 newly attributes Gemma 3's adjusted ranking losses partly to verbosity and explains perfect filtering accuracy through default phrasing and explicit geolocation cues. Its new Limitations section acknowledges geographic participation bias and difficulty measuring individual-user influence without identifiers.

D1.justification: v4 supplies the classifier instruction, output schema, and fuller consent details. It removes the explicit GeoArena-1K release subsection and dedicated reproducibility commitments concerning complete code/data and deployment documentation. The repository link and model specifications remain; these documentation changes do not establish that resources were withdrawn.

R1.justification: Related work expands from geolocalization methods and benchmarks to broader geographic reasoning, adding GEOBench-VLM, MapEval, geometry/topology evaluation, and GeoChain. Table 1 introduces reasoning-oriented and label-free distinctions, while the introduction explicitly positions GeoArena relative to preference-based arenas in other domains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, system description, results discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around geographic reasoning. v4 adds a Problem Definition section, reorders related work and result subsections, expands the appendices, and removes the standalone dataset-release and reproducibility sections.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a two-column layout, redraws the system diagram, restructures the benchmark-comparison table, and moves model specifications to the appendix. Dataset composition changes from a table to doughnut charts; style coefficients move into prose; an adjusted leaderboard is added. Existing case figures are regrouped and relocated.

improvement.justification: The added style-adjusted leaderboard makes consequential ranking confounds visible beyond v3's coefficient analysis, and the concrete participation-bias limitations improve transparency. These provide a limited net quality gain. Benefits are tempered by unclear filtering deployment, less explicit data-release commitments, and little new direct validation of the broader geographic-reasoning claims.
